reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) demonstrates that CeO2 nanorods with (110) facets enable synthesis of sub-nanometer CoNiCuZnPd HEA clusters and show structural reversibility under redox cycling, but it does not provide data on interfacial bonding constraining atomic mobility, suppressing phase segregation at high temperatures, or comparative behavior of free-standing nanoparticles. The key mechanistic premises about diffusion suppression and stability across 473–1923 K are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: CeO2 nanorods with (110) facets provide strong interfacial bonding with HEA nanoparticles
This interfacial bonding constrains atomic mobility in the nanoparticles
Constrained atomic mobility suppresses diffusion-driven phase segregation
Free-standing nanoparticles lack this interfacial constraint and thus exhibit higher atomic diffusion
The hypothesis applies to CoNiCuZnPd HEA nanoparticles across 473–1923 K
